entries.label: balancing_set
entries.why: Explained. Cell E_NFPR <- E_NBFC: 16,674 -> 22,308 (5,634, +33.8%; 6 entries). Largest moves: fincorp R8 dividends 2,731 (+44.0%); fincorp R4 mf_lookthrough 2,329 (+44.0%); fincorp R4 borrowings 324 (+9.5%); fincorp R8 mf_lookthrough 102 (+44.0%); fincorp R4 bonds 88 (+9.5%). The largest mover is explained under its entry: E_BANK ran a -1,02,838 deficit and E_NBFC a 2,32,893 surplus in the prior (fincorp-2): FISIM leaves banks' SNA property income negative, while the F4a GOS split (NAS 8.12 S125-S127 GVA, including MFs, auxiliaries and captive institutions) gives NBFCs more GOS than the RTP-scaled interest matrix can carry. E_NBFC's onward distribution of the private NFC equity it holds (holding companies) is only the ratio-based prior (fincorp-2), so its dividends and MF-looked-through payments rising is toward the evidence.

entries.label: balancing_set
entries.why: Unexplained (fincorp-37, Checkpoint B). Cell E_NFPU <- E_BANK: 48,449 -> 30,382 (-18,067, -37.3%; 3 entries). Largest moves: fincorp R4 deposits -17,622 (-37.3%); fincorp R4 bonds -440 (-37.3%); fincorp R8 dividends -5 (-84.5%). Public NFCs' deposit interest from banks is FSF deposits x the scaled cost of deposits (medium). E_NFPU's prior keeps 3,12,829 over NAS 2026 St 1.9 public NFC saving (closure institution_gaps). Its cause is not a documented source disagreement: the old-base NAS 2024 St 2.1A shows departmental enterprises passing 95.6% of their primary income on as D6 + D7 (1,48,177 in 2022-23), a flow the new-base SAM does not write (government-33, a NAD question for Checkpoint B). After the Wave C constraints held the published outlets (R9d at the AFS total, R18 at IGAS-2, T4a within 25% of the old-base share, R7x lines and payer shares, insurers' and MF bond interest near FSF stock x coupon, non-government dividends near the R7-grossed issuer total), what is left of the surplus lands on E_NFPU's remaining weak-keyed flows (fincorp-32, -37).
